ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two concentric circles with radii 1 and 9 form an annulus. $n$ circles without overlap are drawn inside this annulus, where every circle touches both circles of the annulus. (The diagram shows an example for $\mathrm{n}=1$ and the other radii as given.) What is the biggest possible value of $n$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a large outer circle and a smaller concentric inner circle, with one example circle in the annular region tangent to both the inner and outer circles. Reasoning: Let O be the common center of the two annulus circles. For any drawn circle, let its radius be r and its center be C. Since the drawn circle is tangent to the inner circle of radius 1, OC = r + 1. Since it is internally tangent to the outer circle of radius 9, OC = 9 - r. Therefore r + 1 = 9 - r, so 2r = 8 and r = 4. Then OC = 5, so every possible center C lies on the circle of radius 5 centered at O. For two such drawn circles, if their centers subtend an angle theta at O, the distance between centers is 2·5·sin(theta/2) = 10 sin(theta/2). Non-overlap requires this distance to be at least 8, so 10 sin(theta/2) >= 8, giving sin(theta/2) >= 4/5 and theta >= 2 arcsin(4/5), about 106.26 degrees. Around 360 degrees, four centers would require total angular separation at least 4·106.26 > 360 degrees, impossible. Thus at most 3 circles can fit. Three circles are possible by placing their centers 120 degrees apart; then each center distance is 10 sin 60° = 5√3 > 8, so they do not overlap. Therefore the biggest possible value of n is 3.

method.method_draft: Let O be the common center of the two annulus circles. For any drawn circle, call its radius r and its center C. Since it is tangent to the inner circle of radius 1, OC = r + 1; since it is internally tangent to the outer circle of radius 9, OC = 9 - r. Solving gives r = 4 and OC = 5, so all possible circle centers lie on the circle of radius 5 centered at O. For two such circles whose centers subtend angle theta at O, their center distance is 2*5*sin(theta/2). Non-overlap requires this distance to be at least 8, so theta >= 2 arcsin(4/5), about 106.26 degrees. Around a full 360 degrees, at most floor(360/106.26) = 3 centers can be placed. Three are possible by placing the centers 120 degrees apart, since their mutual distance is 10 sin 60 = 5sqrt(3) > 8. Therefore the maximum n is 3.

method.method_draft: Again let O be the common center. If an admissible circle has radius r and center C, tangency to the inner and outer annulus circles gives OC = 1 + r and OC = 9 - r, hence r = 4 and OC = 5. Thus every admissible circle is a radius-4 circle whose center lies on the circle of radius 5 about O. To rule out 4 circles, suppose four centers were placed on that radius-5 circle. The four angular gaps around O sum to 360 degrees, so at least one gap is at most 90 degrees. The two centers bordering that gap are then at distance at most the chord for 90 degrees, namely 5sqrt(2), which is less than 8. But distance less than 8 means the two radius-4 circles overlap, impossible. Hence n <= 3. To realize n = 3, place three centers 120 degrees apart on the radius-5 circle; their pairwise distances are 5sqrt(3) > 8, so the corresponding radius-4 circles do not overlap and each still touches both annulus boundaries. Therefore the maximum is 3.

Because it is tangent to the inner radius-1 circle and the outer radius-9 circle, OC=1+r and OC=9-r, so r=4 and OC=5. Thus every such circle has radius 4 and its center lies on the circle of radius 5 centered at O.

If two such circles are disjoint, the distance between their centers must be at least 8. Now place n centers on the radius-5 circle. For n=4, the 4 central gaps around O sum to 360°, so one gap is at most 90°. The chord between the two centers bordering that gap is at most 5\sqrt2, which is less than 8, so those two radius-4 circles would overlap. Hence n cannot be 4 or more, so n<=3.

To realize n=3, place the centers 120° apart on the radius-5 circle. Then each pair of centers is separated by chord length 5\sqrt3>8, so the three radius-4 circles are disjoint and each touches both annulus boundaries. Therefore the maximum possible value is 3.
